title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Allowance for an Owner Who Has Kept Paying
content:
## Training Q&A: the prompt settlement allowance

**Who earns it?** A prompt settlement allowance is allowed, on a settlement of a Preventive Maintenance Agreements record, to an owner who has kept paying through the term. Two readings decide it: the payments received on the agreement, and the whole months of its term that have run at the settlement day.

**How much?**

| Payments received on the agreement | Whole months of the term run at the settlement day | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | more than 6 | the established prompt allowance, 60.00 USD |
| 2 or more | no more than 6 | the prompt settlement allowance, 30.00 USD |
| fewer than 2 | any | no prompt settlement allowance |

**Where do the boundaries fall?** At exactly 2 payments received the owner is in the first two rows, not the third. At exactly 6 whole months run the term is "no more than 6", so the allowance is 30.00 USD; at 7 whole months it is 60.00 USD.

**Does a larger payment count for more?** No; the reading is the number of payments received on the agreement, not their amounts.

**Worked case (hypothetical).** An agreement carrying 4 payments received, settled 8 whole months into its term: the established prompt allowance of 60.00 USD is allowed. The same agreement settled 5 whole months into its term: 30.00 USD.
